taxonomy.subtopic: Autoreactive lymphocytes and CNS oligodendrocyte injury

questions.stem_html:
A 28-year-old woman has painful loss of vision in one eye that improves over several weeks. Eight months later she develops diplopia; examination shows impaired adduction of the left eye with nystagmus of the abducting right eye. MRI reveals periventricular ovoid lesions, and cerebrospinal fluid contains oligoclonal IgG bands.

Which cellular target is primarily damaged in this disorder?

options.text_html: Schwann cells and peripheral nerve roots
Oligodendrocytes and central nervous system myelin

questions.explanation_html: Multiple sclerosis is an immune-mediated inflammatory demyelinating disease of the CNS. Oligodendrocyte and myelin injury causes lesions disseminated in time and space, including optic neuritis and internuclear ophthalmoplegia. The clinical relapses, periventricular plaques, and oligoclonal bands localize the process to CNS myelin made by oligodendrocytes.

wrong_choice_explanations.1: Peripheral demyelination with root involvement is characteristic of Guillain-Barré syndrome or CIDP.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: Anterior horn-cell degeneration causes pure lower motor neuron weakness without optic neuritis or CNS plaques.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Loss of striatal neurons is characteristic of Huntington disease.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Acetylcholine-receptor disease causes fatigable weakness without central lesions or sensory pathways.

questions.educational_objective: Differentiate CNS from peripheral demyelination by linking optic neuritis, internuclear ophthalmoplegia, periventricular plaques, and oligoclonal bands to oligodendrocyte injury.
